cards.question: About how much does stall speed increase in a 45° coordinated bank?
cards.answer: Load factor ≈ 1.4 g, so stall speed rises by about √1.4 ≈ 18%.

cards.question: What is the load factor in a 60° bank level turn, and roughly the stall speed increase?
cards.answer: 2 g; stall speed about 41% higher (√2).

cards.question: What is the dry adiabatic lapse rate used in soaring discussions?
cards.answer: About 3°C per 1,000 ft (≈5.4°F / 1,000 ft).

cards.question: What three ingredients are required for a thunderstorm?
cards.answer: Unstable air + lifting action + moisture (humidity).

cards.question: Rough rule for cumulus base (AGL) using °F?
cards.answer: (Temperature − dew point) / 4.4 × 1,000 = approximate base AGL.

cards.question: Do glider pilots need an FAA medical certificate?
cards.answer: No. But under 61.53 you must not fly with a known medical deficiency that makes you unsafe.
choices: No medical, but 61.53 fitness still applies

cards.question: Minimum ages: solo glider and Private Pilot — Glider?
cards.answer: Solo 14; Private Pilot glider 16.

cards.question: To carry passengers in a glider, what recent experience is required?
cards.answer: Three takeoffs and landings in a glider within the preceding 90 days (61.57), plus a current flight review as applicable.

cards.question: What does IMSAFE stand for?
cards.answer: Illness, Medication, Stress, Alcohol, Fatigue, Emotion.

cards.question: Name the five hazardous attitudes and one antidote example.
cards.answer: Anti-authority → follow the rules; Impulsivity → not so fast; Invulnerability → it could happen to me; Macho → taking chances is foolish; Resignation → I can make a difference.

cards.question: Class G day below 1,200 AGL — basic VFR for a glider?
cards.answer: 1 SM visibility, clear of clouds.

cards.question: How does 91.215 treat gliders in the Mode C veil (30 NM App. D)?
cards.answer: A glider may operate unequipped if outside A/B/C and below the B/C ceiling or 10,000 MSL, whichever is lower.

cards.question: Does the 'above 10,000 MSL' Mode C rule apply to gliders?
cards.answer: No — 91.215(b)(5) excepts aircraft without an engine-driven electrical system, balloons, and gliders (excluding ≤2,500 AGL carve-out language for powered ships).

cards.question: Private deck not loaded yet — what do you do?
cards.answer: Use Import to upload CSV/JSON with track=private when your private study Q&A are ready (planned last after CFI-G).

cards.question: What does 61.133 allow a commercial glider pilot to do?
cards.answer: Act as PIC of a glider carrying persons or property for compensation or hire; exercise commercial privileges in the glider category (not airplane privileges in a glider).

cards.question: 61.129(f)(2) path if you already have 200 hours heavier-than-air — key numbers?
cards.answer: 20 glider PIC flights; 3 hours dual or 10 training flights including 3 prep flights in the 2 calendar months before the test month; 5 solo flights on 61.127(b)(6) areas.

cards.question: Adding glider to an existing commercial airplane certificate — knowledge test?
cards.answer: Generally no new knowledge test under 61.63 for the additional category rating; you still take the commercial glider practical test (PTS 23B additional-rating table).

cards.question: Why can a club commercial pilot charge for glider demo rides without Part 119?
cards.answer: 14 CFR 119.1(e)(5) excepts nonstop commercial air tours in an airplane or glider within 25 SM of takeoff (sightseeing). 91.147 / Part 136 do not apply to gliders; 91.409(b) 100-hour still applies when carrying persons for hire.

cards.question: When is a 100-hour inspection required for a glider?
cards.answer: When carrying persons for hire (instruction for hire or paid sightseeing) — 91.409(b). Annual still required.

cards.question: INOP equipment on a 2-33 without an MEL — which rule?
cards.answer: 91.213(d): remove or deactivate, placard, and determine it is not a hazard. Required instruments (e.g., ASI per SFM) must work.

cards.question: Is towline / rope break on the commercial glider practical test?
cards.answer: Yes. FAA-S-8081-23B Area IV Task G (Aerotow — Abnormal Occurrences) includes towline break and related abnormals; evaluator may simulate.

cards.question: What is boxing the wake?
cards.answer: On tow, maneuver slightly outside the towplane’s wake in a rectangular pattern while maintaining control and coordination (PTS IV.E). GFH: not below 1,000 AGL.

cards.question: 91.309 towline strength window and weak-link rule?
cards.answer: Towline ≥200 ft; strength 80–200% of glider max certificated operating weight. If rope is stronger than twice MGW, use glider-end safety link (80–200% MGW) and stronger towplane-end link (≤25% greater than glider-end link, ≤2× MGW).

cards.question: Glider and towplane both fail to release — how is it tested?
cards.answer: Oral only on the commercial PTS (IV.G). Discuss signals, low-tow on final, glider lands first.

cards.question: Commercial landing touchdown/stop standard?
cards.answer: Touch in the designated area; stop short of and within 100 ft of the designated point without rolling past it (light–medium brake).
choices: Within 100 ft, not past the point

cards.question: Commercial slips task — key points?
cards.answer: Evaluator picks one type (forward/side/turning). Demonstrate slip without drag devices; maintain track; 2-33 SFM: initiate recovery so you are out of the slip by 50 ft remaining.

cards.question: Stall recognition/recovery completion altitude on commercial glider PTS?
cards.answer: Select an entry altitude that allows completion no lower than 1,500 ft AGL. Recover at first buffet or rapid decay of control effectiveness.

cards.question: Steep turn standard (commercial glider)?
cards.answer: 720° turn, 45° ±5° bank, airspeed ±5 kt, rollout on entry heading ±10°.

cards.question: PTS three-way exchange of flight controls wording?
cards.answer: “You have the flight controls” / “I have the flight controls” / “You have the flight controls,” then a visual check.

cards.question: What must you demonstrate for minimum sink and speed-to-fly?
cards.answer: Know the concepts; determine and maintain each selected speed ±5 knots (PTS V).

cards.question: XC planning glide ratio for a 2-33 — published L/D vs planning figure?
cards.answer: Published L/D ~23:1; plan about half (≈11:1 / ~2 NM per 1,000 ft) so you still make a field.

cards.question: How is simulated off-airport landing flown on the commercial test?
cards.answer: At an established airport, without using the altimeter. Field selection knowledge is oral.

cards.question: Airplane commercial → glider add-on: which areas are NONE / skipped on the required table?
cards.answer: Navigation (VIII) is NONE. Also typically skip I.A Certificates and II.D Flight Deck Management and III.A/C — but the evaluator may still sample skipped tasks. Prepare them.

cards.question: CFI-G Q&A bank empty — next step?
cards.answer: When you start CFI-G study, upload FOI and instructor Q&A via Import (CSV/JSON, track=cfi_g). Do this before building the private deck.

cards.question: FOI stub: what are the four levels of learning?
cards.answer: Rote → Understanding → Application → Correlation. (Expand with your uploaded FOI deck later.)

cards.question: 2-33 never-exceed / max aero-tow / max dive-or-glide speed?
cards.answer: 98 mph (placarded).

cards.question: 2-33 max auto/winch tow speed?
cards.answer: 69 mph.

cards.question: 2-33 normal approach speed rule (SFM)?
cards.answer: 55 mph + 1 mph for each 1 mph of wind. (Discard “half the wind” mnemonics that conflict with the SFM.)

cards.question: Approximate 2-33 stall speeds solo vs dual (SFM)?
cards.answer: About 34 mph solo / 38 mph dual; dive brakes add ~2 mph.

cards.question: 2-33 best L/D speed and published glide ratio?
cards.answer: Best L/D about 50 mph; published L/D about 23:1. Min-sink ~42 mph.

cards.question: 2-33 limit and ultimate load factors?
cards.answer: Limit +4.67 / −2.56 g; ultimate +7.0 / −3.8 g.

cards.question: 2-33 demonstrated / placarded crosswind?
cards.answer: 17 mph (per SFM notes used at FLF).

cards.question: 2-33 maximum gross weight?
Weak-link strength window for a 2-33 at 1,040 lb MGW?
cards.answer: 80–200% → 832–2,080 lb. Verify the actual rope/link tags on the ship.

cards.question: SFM slip recovery height remaining?
cards.answer: Initiate recovery so at least 50 ft AGL remains when recovering from the slip.

cards.question: Tow-hook release check force (SFM)?
cards.answer: About 5–20 lb on the nose/CG hook check — verify with SFM in hand.

cards.question: FLF yellow 2-33A vs white 2-33 trim difference?
cards.answer: Yellow 2-33A: bungee trim and larger aerodynamically balanced rudder. White 2-33: ratchet trim.

cards.question: List the current Schweizer 2-33 airframe ADs to verify in the logbook.
cards.answer: 76-13-11 R1 (drain holes, S/N 1–424, one-time); 77-23-10 (fin spar attach, recurring unless terminated); 87-02-01 (tow-release inspect, 100 hr); 87-17-01 (replace welded-lug arms, one-time). 97-08-06 R1 L’Hotellier dropped 2-33.

cards.question: What aircraft documents must you locate for the practical test?
cards.answer: Airworthiness certificate, registration, operating limitations/placards/SFM, W&B and equipment list, maintenance/AD compliance status.
